user.passage: These arrangements, which had won the admiration of all the critics, were put into execution on 3 Vendemiaire, Year VIII (25 September 1799), at five in the morning. Preparations for the crossing had been made near the village of Dietikon with extraordinary care and secrecy. Boats had been dragged by hand and hidden in the woods. By morning they were afloat, and the troops were silently drawn up on the bank. General Foy, later distinguished as an orator, commanded the artillery in this memorable battle; he positioned several batteries to protect the crossing. Six hundred men boldly embarked and reached the opposite bank. They immediately attacked and scattered the enemy skirmishers. Korsakoff had stationed three battalions with artillery there, on the plateau of Closter-Fahr. Our artillery, skilfully directed, soon silenced the Russian guns and protected the successive crossings of our advance guard. When General Gazan had assembled sufficient reinforcements with the six hundred men who had crossed first, he advanced against the three Russian battalions guarding Closter-Fahr. They had established themselves in a wood and defended it bravely. Gazan surrounded them and had to kill almost every last man to dislodge them. Once these three battalions had been destroyed, the bridge was laid. The rest of Lorge's division and part of Mesnard's division crossed the Limmat: fifteen thousand men had been brought across the river. Bontemps's brigade was stationed at Regensdorf to face Durasof should he move up from the lower Limmat. The main body, directed by chief of staff Oudinot, moved upstream along the Limmat to reach the rear of Zurich.
user.question: After the bridge was laid and the main crossing completed, where was Bontemps's brigade stationed to face Durasof, rather than following Oudinot upstream?

user.passage: Once this part of the operation was completed, Massena personally returned to the other bank of the Limmat to oversee the movements of his wings. On his right, Mortier had advanced towards Zurich by way of Wollishofen, but had encountered Korsakoff's main force, positioned, as already stated, in front of the Limmat, and had been compelled to fall back. Arriving at that moment, Massena set Klein's division, which was at Altstetten, in motion. Humbert, at the head of his four thousand grenadiers, marched on Zurich and restored the battle. Mortier renewed his attacks, and the Russians were thus confined within Zurich.
user.question: Where was Klein's division stationed immediately before Massena set it in motion, rather than where Humbert subsequently marched?
